packet.title: Checkout fails only on orders above roughly 1,000 USD-equivalent since payment-service deploy d6 (enhanced fraud screening), 2026-08-11T13:36Z
packet.impact: 12 merchants, 13 tickets, 2026-08-11T14:14Z through 2026-08-14T11:05Z, all currently unresolved on day four (t248). Two sampled accounts are enterprise NA contracts worth about $240k (Northwind Retail, a01) and about $190k (Cardinal Foods, a10) — a10 has flagged P1 with revenue blocked (t230), a01 has filed twice and self-reports at least about $18k in abandoned carts (t223, t248). Affected merchants span NA, EU and JP-facing currencies (t224, t226, t238). Because the defect targets high-value orders specifically, revenue lost per failure is disproportionately large, and at least one confirmed sale went to a competitor (t235). ACV exposure is understated: 10 of 12 accounts were not pulled.

evidence.text: Deploy d6 (payment-service, "Enable enhanced fraud screening for high-value transactions") shipped 2026-08-11T13:36Z; first customer report says failures began "about 2:15 this afternoon" — roughly a 40-minute gap.
Independent monitoring corroboration: POST /v2/transactions returning 500s "since Tuesday afternoon," and "only requests above four figures seem affected."

Paired same-merchant pass/fail tests isolate the variable to order value: €1,250 / €1,900 / €4,100 failed while a €40 test succeeded; above ¥150,000 fails while smaller consumer orders are unaffected; 40+ seat licenses fail while a 5-seat purchase succeeded; a $1,300 patio set fails while cheaper items go through.
Additional threshold data points: $1,600 and $2,050 orders, a $2,300 cart, five-figure B2B carts, bookings over €1,000, two orders over $1,000.
Failure occurs before the card network: banks "show no charge attempt at all" despite customers seeing declines.
Two observed shapes on the same endpoint — hard 500s versus about 30-second timeouts, endless spinners and white screens.
Not client-side: reproduced on Chrome and Edge, Safari/iPhone and Firefox, Chrome and Safari.
Not pre-existing: no archived checkout-failure tickets; archived checkout hits were a gift-message how-to, an expired discount code and a rate-limit question, all non-defects.

Weaker alternative deploy d5 (web-storefront seasonal CSS/theme, 2026-08-09T11:20Z) shipped about 2 days earlier with no reports in the interim and cannot explain server-side 500s or amount-dependent behaviour.

packet.suggested_repro: On any merchant storefront, build a cart just under and just over about 1,000 USD-equivalent and submit both through Place Order (POST /v2/transactions). Expect the sub-threshold order to succeed and the over-threshold order to either return HTTP 500 or hang for about 30 seconds and then time out with no charge attempt reaching the issuer (t224, t228, t238, t246). Repeat in a non-USD currency — e.g. about €1,000+ or about ¥150,000+ — to check whether the threshold is evaluated post-FX-conversion rather than on the raw numeric amount (t233, t238). Then re-run the same two carts with d6's enhanced fraud screening disabled; if the over-threshold order succeeds, the correlation is confirmed.
packet.not_examined: No code, logs, or deploy diff access; the trace attached to t228 was not read. Deploys after 2026-08-11T15:00Z were not queried, so we cannot say whether remediation or a further payment-service change has shipped (t248 suggests it has not). Accounts for 10 of 12 customers (a02–a09, a11, a12) were not pulled, so ACV exposure is understated. The fraud-screening vendor's latency/error rate, timeout configuration and threshold settings were not examined, nor was any transaction ledger checked for orphaned authorizations on hung requests. Root cause is unconfirmed — this is a timing and population correlation only. Concurrent analytics/reporting timeouts (t236, t240, t247) were not investigated and are treated as a separate incident.
packet.merged_note: No single ticket states the boundary, but read together the reported amounts converge on one number: the highest confirmed successes are about €40, a 5-seat licence and "cheaper items" (t224, t241, t246), while the lowest confirmed failures are about €1,000, about $1,000 and about $1,300 (t233, t243, t246). Critically, the JPY boundary is reported at about ¥150,000 — roughly $1,000 equivalent, not a raw numeric 1,000 (t238). Across four currencies the cutoff therefore sits at approximately 1,000 USD-equivalent, which implies a single currency-agnostic threshold evaluated after FX conversion. That converted-threshold shape is invisible in any one ticket and only appears when the USD, EUR and JPY reports are placed side by side (t224, t226, t233, t238, t243, t246).
